stem: Indo-Islamic architecture developed in India after the establishment of the __________.
solution: Indo-Islamic architecture developed with the Delhi Sultanate from the 13th century.

stem: A key structural feature introduced by Indo-Islamic architecture was the __________.
solution: Indo-Islamic architecture introduced the true arch and the dome to India.

stem: The Qutb Minar in Delhi was begun by __________.
solution: The Qutb Minar was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.

stem: The Qutb Minar was built as a __________.
solution: The Qutb Minar is a victory tower and minaret attached to a mosque.

stem: The Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, the earliest surviving mosque of the Delhi Sultanate, reused material from __________.
solution: The Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque was built using pillars and material from demolished temples.

stem: The Alai Darwaza, a gateway with a true dome, was built by __________.
solution: The Alai Darwaza was built by Alauddin Khalji.

stem: The garden-tomb layout with a tomb in the centre of a four-part garden is called a __________.
solution: The charbagh is a four-quartered garden layout, central to Mughal tombs.

stem: The first great Mughal garden-tomb, and a forerunner of the Taj Mahal, is __________.
solution: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi was the first great Mughal garden-tomb.

stem: The Taj Mahal at Agra was built by the emperor __________.
solution: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

stem: The Taj Mahal is built mainly of __________.
solution: The Taj Mahal is built of white marble.

stem: The technique of inlaying semi-precious stones into marble, used in the Taj Mahal, is called __________.
solution: Pietra dura (parchin kari) is the stone-inlay technique used in the Taj Mahal.

stem: Fatehpur Sikri, a planned city, was built by the emperor __________.
solution: Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar as his capital.

stem: The massive gateway at Fatehpur Sikri, one of the tallest in India, is the __________.
solution: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri is one of the tallest gateways.

stem: The Buland Darwaza was built to commemorate Akbar's victory over __________.
solution: The Buland Darwaza commemorates Akbar's conquest of Gujarat.

stem: The tomb of Akbar is located at __________.
solution: Akbar's tomb is at Sikandra near Agra.

stem: The 'iwan' in Indo-Islamic architecture is a __________.
options: large vaulted arched hall/recess open on one side
solution: An iwan is a large vaulted arched recess or hall open on one side.

stem: The open courtyard of a mosque is called the __________.
solution: The sahn is the open courtyard of a mosque.

stem: The niche in a mosque wall indicating the direction of Mecca is the __________.
solution: The mihrab is the niche indicating the qibla (direction of Mecca).

stem: The pulpit in a mosque from which the sermon is delivered is the __________.
solution: The minbar is the pulpit for delivering the sermon.

stem: The Jama Masjid of Delhi, one of the largest mosques in India, was built by __________.
solution: The Jama Masjid of Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.

stem: The Red Fort (Lal Qila) in Delhi was built by __________.
solution: The Red Fort of Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.

stem: The construction technique that avoids the true arch by overlapping stone courses is the __________ (corbelling).
solution: The indigenous trabeate (corbelled) method uses overlapping courses instead of a true arch.

stem: The true arch works on the principle of the __________.
solution: The true (arcuate) arch uses wedge-shaped voussoirs locked by a keystone.

stem: A double dome, with an outer and inner shell, was used to __________.
options: give a grand exterior while keeping a proportionate interior
solution: The double dome allows a tall grand exterior with a well-proportioned interior height.

stem: The Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur, famous for its huge dome, is the tomb of __________.
solution: The Gol Gumbaz is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah of Bijapur.

stem: The Gol Gumbaz is famous for its 'whispering gallery', which is an example of __________.
solution: The whispering gallery of Gol Gumbaz is a marvel of acoustic engineering.

stem: The Charminar, with four minarets, is located at __________.
solution: The Charminar is in Hyderabad, built by the Qutb Shahi ruler.

stem: Provincial styles of Indo-Islamic architecture developed in regions like Bengal, Gujarat, Malwa and __________.
solution: Distinct provincial styles arose in Bengal, Gujarat, Malwa, Jaunpur and the Deccan.

stem: The Atala Masjid and other mosques with tall arched screens belong to the __________ provincial style.
solution: The Atala Masjid belongs to the Jaunpur (Sharqi) style, noted for its bold arched screens.

stem: Bengal's Indo-Islamic architecture is distinctive for its __________.
solution: Bengal style is known for curved bangla roofs and terracotta ornamentation.

stem: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri at Sasaram stands in the middle of a __________.
solution: Sher Shah Suri's tomb at Sasaram stands on an island in a large tank (lake).

stem: The chhatri (domed kiosk) and jharokha (projecting balcony) were features borrowed from __________ architecture.
solution: The chhatri and jharokha were indigenous (Rajput) features absorbed into Indo-Islamic style.

stem: The use of __________ (perforated stone screens) is a hallmark of Indo-Islamic architecture.
solution: Jali (perforated stone screens) are a hallmark decorative feature.

stem: Indo-Islamic architecture is characterised by decoration using __________ rather than figures.
solution: Islamic decoration avoids figures, using geometric, floral and calligraphic ornament.

stem: The calligraphy on Indo-Islamic buildings usually consists of verses from the __________.
solution: The calligraphic inscriptions are usually Quranic verses.

stem: The Taj Mahal complex is laid out as a __________.
options: charbagh with the tomb at the northern end
solution: The Taj Mahal is set in a charbagh, with the tomb placed at the northern end (not centre).

stem: The Mughal style reached its peak of refinement under __________.
solution: Mughal architecture reached its zenith under Shah Jahan.

stem: The architecture that blends Persian, Central Asian and Indian traditions is called __________.
solution: The synthesis of Persian, Central Asian and Indian styles is called Indo-Islamic architecture.

stem: The four tall towers around the Taj Mahal are __________.
solution: Four minarets stand at the corners of the Taj Mahal platform.

stem: The building material red sandstone was widely used in the architecture of __________.
solution: Red sandstone was extensively used in Akbar's buildings like Fatehpur Sikri and Agra Fort.

stem: The transition from red sandstone to white marble in Mughal architecture is best seen from Akbar's to __________'s buildings.
solution: The shift from red sandstone to white marble is seen from Akbar's to Shah Jahan's buildings.

stem: The Diwan-i-Am and Diwan-i-Khas in Mughal forts were halls of __________.
solution: The Diwan-i-Am (public) and Diwan-i-Khas (private) were audience halls.

stem: The Panch Mahal at Fatehpur Sikri is a __________ structure.
solution: The Panch Mahal is a five-storeyed open pavilion at Fatehpur Sikri.

stem: The tomb of Itmad-ud-Daulah at Agra is important as an early example of __________.
solution: Itmad-ud-Daulah's tomb ('Baby Taj') is an early example of marble pietra dura inlay.

stem: A dome usually rests on a transitional zone of __________ that converts a square base to a circle.
solution: Squinches or pendentives transition a square chamber to a circular dome base.

stem: The tradition of building __________ (stepwells) also continued in the Indo-Islamic period.
solution: Baolis (stepwells) continued to be built in the Indo-Islamic period.

stem: The Lodi Gardens in Delhi contain tombs of the __________ dynasty.
solution: The Lodi Gardens contain the tombs of the Sayyid and Lodi rulers.

stem: The octagonal tomb form of the Sultanate period is well seen in the tomb of __________.
options: Sher Shah Suri (and earlier the Sayyid/Lodi tombs)
solution: The octagonal tomb type is seen in the Sur and Sayyid/Lodi tombs.

stem: Indo-Islamic architecture is significant because it represents a __________ of building traditions.
solution: Indo-Islamic architecture represents a rich synthesis of Indian and Islamic traditions.

stem: The Taj Mahal is recognised as a __________.
solution: The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
